notesEn.formation: Verb Stem + ~고 있다 (Conjugates to ~고 있어요 / ~고 있습니다).
notesEn.usage: Indicates an action currently in progress at the time of speaking.
notesEn.nuance: Applies directly to active verbs regardless of whether the stem ends in a vowel or consonant.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar Kata Kerja + ~고 있다 (Dikonjugasikan menjadi ~고 있어요 / ~고 있습니다).
notesId.usage: Menunjukkan tindakan yang sedang berlangsung pada saat berbicara.
notesId.nuance: Berlaku langsung untuk kata kerja aktif tanpa memandang apakah kata dasar berakhiran vokal atau konsonan.

examples.meaningEn: I am listening to music right now.
My friend is eating a meal.

quiz.question: How do you conjugate '공부하다' (to study) into the present continuous polite form?
quiz.explanationEn: Attach ~고 있다 to the stem 공부하, yielding 공부하고 있어요 in informal polite style.
quiz.explanationId: Tempelkan ~고 있다 pada kata dasar 공부하, menghasilkan 공부하고 있어요 dalam gaya sopan informal.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I am listening to music right now. -> 지금 음악을 듣___ 있어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach the particle suffix connecting the verb stem to 있다.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran partikel yang menghubungkan kata dasar kata kerja ke 있다.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'What are you doing?'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Apa yang sedang kamu lakukan?'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use what (무엇을) + do stem (하) + continuous (고 있어요?).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan apa (무엇을) + kata dasar lakukan (하) + sedang berlangsung (고 있어요?).

notesEn.formation: Verb Stem + ~고 있었다 (Conjugates to ~고 있었어요 / ~고 있었습니다).
notesEn.usage: Expresses an action that was ongoing at a specific point in the past.
notesEn.nuance: Combines the continuous aspect suffix ~고 with past tense auxiliary 있었다.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar Kata Kerja + ~고 있었다 (Dikonjugasikan menjadi ~고 있었어요 / ~고 있었습니다).
notesId.usage: Mengekspresikan tindakan yang sedang berlangsung pada titik waktu tertentu di masa lalu.
notesId.nuance: Menggabungkan akhiran aspek keberlanjutan ~고 dengan kata kerja bantu masa lalu 있었다.

examples.meaningEn: I was reading a book at that time.
examples.meaningId: Saya sedang membaca buku pada saat itu.

examples.meaningEn: I was sleeping when you called.
examples.meaningId: Saya sedang tidur ketika kamu menelepon.

quiz.question: Which form translates to 'was sleeping'?
quiz.explanationEn: 자다 stem (자) + ~고 있었어요 indicates past continuous action.
quiz.explanationId: Kata dasar 자다 (자) + ~고 있었어요 menunjukkan tindakan yang dulu sedang berlangsung.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I was reading a book. -> 책을 읽고 ___.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Use past continuous auxiliary ending in informal polite style.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Gunakan akhiran bantu masa lalu sedang berlangsung dalam gaya sopan informal.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I was reading a book at that time.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya sedang membaca buku pada saat itu.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use at that time (그때) + book (책을) + read (읽) + past continuous (고 있었어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan pada saat itu (그때) + buku (책을) + membaca (읽) + lampau berlangsung (고 있었어요).

meaningId: Partikel subjek dan topik bentuk honorifik (penghormatan).

notesEn.usage: Used when the subject of the sentence is a person of higher status or elder relative deserving respect.
notesEn.nuance: Demonstrates respect directly to the subject performing the action.

notesId.usage: Digunakan ketika subjek kalimat adalah seseorang dengan status lebih tinggi atau kerabat lebih tua yang dihormati.
notesId.nuance: Menunjukkan rasa hormat secara langsung kepada subjek yang melakukan tindakan.

quiz.question: Which particle respectfully replaces '~이/가' for honored subjects like '선생님'?
quiz.explanationEn: ~께서 replaces standard subject particles ~이/가 when referring to respected subjects.
quiz.explanationId: ~께서 menggantikan partikel subjek standar ~이/가 saat merujuk pada subjek yang dihormati.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean using honorific particle: 'The teacher arrived.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea menggunakan partikel honorifik: 'Guru telah datang.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use teacher (선생님) + honorific subject particle (께서) + arrived (오셨습니다).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan guru (선생님) + partikel subjek honorifik (께서) + datang lampau (오셨습니다).

meaningEn: Honorific verb infix showing respect to the subject.
meaningId: Sisipan kata kerja honorifik untuk menunjukkan rasa hormat pada subjek.

notesEn.formation: Stem + ~시~ (vowel stem) / ~으시~ (consonant stem). Present informal polite: ~(으)세요.
notesEn.usage: Elevates the subject performing the action or experiencing the state.
notesEn.nuance: Essential for polite dialogue when addressing elders, teachers, customers, or superiors.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar + ~시~ (akhiran vokal) / ~으시~ (akhiran konsonan). Bentuk sopan informal sekarang: ~(으)세요.
notesId.usage: Meninggikan subjek yang melakukan tindakan atau mengalami kondisi.
notesId.nuance: Sangat penting untuk dialog sopan saat berbicara dengan orang tua, guru, pelanggan, atau atasan.

examples.meaningEn: Father is at home (계시다 is honorific of 있다).
examples.meaningId: Ayah ada di rumah (계시다 adalah bentuk honorifik dari 있다).

quiz.question: What is the present informal polite honorific conjugation for '가다' (to go)?
quiz.explanationEn: 가다 stem (가) + honorific ending ~세요 creates 가세요.
quiz.explanationId: Kata dasar 가다 (가) + akhiran honorifik ~세요 membentuk 가세요.

fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran sopan informal honorifik sekarang.

meaningEn: Special honorific vocabulary words (드시다, 계시다, 주무시다, etc.).
meaningId: Kosakata honorifik khusus (드시다, 계시다, 주무시다, dll.).

notesEn.formation: Replaces basic verbs/nouns: 먹다/마시다 -> 드시다, 있다 -> 계시다, 자다 -> 주무시다, 밥 -> 진지, 집 -> 댁.
notesEn.usage: Used instead of adding ~(으)시~ when inherent honorific terms exist.
notesEn.nuance: Always takes precedence over regular verb honorific suffix additions.

notesId.formation: Menggantikan kata kerja/benda dasar: 먹다/마시다 -> 드시다, 있다 -> 계시다, 자다 -> 주무시다, 밥 -> 진지, 집 -> 댁.
notesId.usage: Digunakan daripada menambahkan ~(으)시~ jika kata honorifik bawaan sudah tersedia.
notesId.nuance: Selalu diutamakan daripada penambahan akhiran honorifik pada kata kerja biasa.

examples.meaningEn: I went to the teacher's house.

quiz.question: What is the honorific equivalent of '자다' (to sleep)?
quiz.explanationEn: 주무시다 is the dedicated honorific verb for '자다'.
quiz.explanationId: 주무시다 adalah kata kerja honorifik khusus untuk '자다'.

fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Conjugate honorific verb for sleep in present polite style.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Konjugasikan kata kerja honorifik untuk tidur dalam gaya sopan sekarang.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'Enjoy your meal / Please eat deliciously.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Selamat makan / Silakan makan dengan nikmat.'
